# SEIS Constitution

## SEIS LAW #001 — Single Active Mission Principle

A mission-oriented system is more valuable than a task-oriented system.

SEIS must never execute multiple implementation missions simultaneously.

The system may collect ideas, store future plans, prepare roadmaps and queue future missions.

However, only one mission may be actively executed at a time.

## Mission Lifecycle

Research
→ Analysis
→ Planning
→ Architecture
→ Implementation
→ Validation
→ Documentation
→ Commit
→ Knowledge Capture
→ Completion

## Completion Requirement

Before starting a new mission, the current mission must be:

- completed
- validated
- documented
- committed
- archived in the knowledge system

## Forbidden Behaviors

- unfinished implementation chains
- random context switching
- parallel feature development without governance
- undocumented changes
- skipping validation
- starting a new mission before closing the current one

## Core Principle

Finish before expanding.
Document before forgetting.
Validate before shipping.
Learn before repeating.
Complete before continuing.

One active mission.
One completed result.
Then the next mission.
